title: Light and Festivals
subtitle: Autumn 2 · 6-week overview
summary: Exploring light and dark, different celebrations around the world and how people mark special times with light.

days.title: Lantern Making
days.what: Create simple lanterns using tissue paper, collage and recycled materials. Explore colours, light and how we use lanterns to celebrate.
days.why: To develop creativity and fine motor skills.

days.title: Autumn Leaf Printing
days.what: Explore autumn leaves using paint. Make prints, pictures and patterns. Talk about the different colours, shapes and textures we see in autumn and how the leaves change.
days.why: To explore nature and develop mark making skills.

days.title: Exploring Shadows and Lights
days.what: Use torches, light boxes and dens to explore shadows. Try different objects and see what happens to the shapes. Talk about light and dark.

days.title: Autumn Walk
days.what: Go on an autumn walk. Look for different leaves, seeds and natural treasures. Talk about what we can see, hear and feel. Collect natural items to bring back for exploring and creative activities.
days.why: To develop observation and language skills.

days.title: Festivals Circle Time
days.what: Talk about different festivals around the world such as Diwali, Hanukkah, Christmas and Chinese New Year. Share stories, pictures and music.
days.why: To develop an understanding of different cultures and celebrations.

days.title: Autumn Baking Activity
days.what: Explore autumn-themed baking. Children help to mix, stir and shape ingredients. Talk about the smells, textures and what happens when it is cooked.
days.why: To develop sensory exploration and early maths skills.

days.title: Autumn Leaf Soup
days.what: Create pretend autumn soup using leaves, water, bowls and spoons. Encourage mixing, pouring and imaginative play. Talk about the different leaves and what happens when we mix them together.
days.why: To encourage imaginative play and language development.

days.title: Leaf Hunt
days.what: Go on a leaf hunt. Look for different leaves and explore their colours, sizes and shapes. Compare the leaves and talk about the changes we see in autumn.
days.why: To develop observation skills and an understanding of the natural world.

days.title: Bakery Role Play
days.what: Set up a pretend bakery where children can make, sell and buy baked goods. Encourage communication, sharing and imaginative play. Talk about different foods and what we might find in a bakery.
days.why: To develop social skills, imagination and language.

days.title: Create Our Own Autumn Pictures
days.what: Use paint, glitter and loose parts to create autumn pictures. Encourage creativity and talk about the colours, textures and shapes we can see in autumn.

days.title: Frozen Animal Rescue – Break Them Out!
days.what: Explore ice and frozen objects. Free animals and small toys from frozen ice. Talk about cold and warm, melting and changing. Develop fine motor skills using tools such as pipettes, spoons and salt.
days.why: To develop problem solving skills and fine motor control.

days.title: Christmas Bakery Playdough Activity
days.what: Use playdoh to make festive treats such as cookies, cakes and biscuits. Explore rolling, cutting and shaping. Talk about different shapes and decorations and what we might see in a bakery.
days.why: To develop creativity, fine motor skills and imaginative play.

days.title: Snowflake Printing
days.what: Create snowflakes using paint and loose parts. Explore different patterns and shapes. Talk about what snowflakes look like and how no two are the same.
days.why: To encourage exploration, creativity and early maths skills.

days.title: Winter Walk / Scavenger Hunt
days.what: Go on a winter walk. Look for signs of winter such as frost, bare trees and natural treasures. Talk about the changes we see in the season and what might be different in winter.
days.why: To develop observation skills and an understanding of the natural world.

days.title: Arctic Animal Ice Tray
days.what: Explore arctic animals using ice, water and small world items. Talk about the animals, where they live and how they stay warm. Encourage imaginative play and language development.
days.why: To develop knowledge and understanding of the world.

other: Focus on kindness, sharing and togetherness.
